info.title: Open Session API
info.description: REST API for Open Session — call-for-speakers forms, submission review, the speaker portal, agenda building, and the public event widgets. Session-cookie auth: sign in via /api/v1/auth (email + one-time code), or use an API key via the Authorization header for server-to-server access.

get.description:
Every event with a published agenda.

The attendee-facing URLs (/sessions, /agenda, …) carry no slug, so the
frontend resolves them through this: one published event means go straight
there, several means show a chooser.

schema.title: Response List Public Events Api V1 Public Events Get

get.description:
Everything the public widgets render, in one unauthenticated payload.

One endpoint rather than five so the sessions list, speakers list, agenda,
itinerary and gallery are guaranteed to agree with each other (EMB-16), and
so a widget costs one request instead of a waterfall.
Serve only headshots belonging to a speaker on the public programme.

post.description:
Go live: mark the event's agenda published and approve scheduled sessions.

Publishing is what hands the schedule to the public widgets, so it also
clears the content-approval gate for anything actually on the calendar —
an organizer who has placed a session has, in practice, approved it.
Place every unscheduled session into the first slot that fits.

get.description: Organizer view: every resource page, draft and published (§8 wiki pages).

Portal view: anyone with a role on this event (speaker, reviewer, admin)
can read the published resource pages — organizer reference material, not
per-person data, so no extra ownership check beyond event membership.

PublicEventSummary.title: PublicEventSummary
PublicEventSummary.description:
Minimal event identity resolvable from a slug with no auth (speaker portal
and public agenda pages need to turn :eventSlug into an id; nothing sensitive).

PublicOption.title: PublicOption
PublicOption.description:
Minimal {id, name} shape for rendering track/format/tag choices on the public
CFP without exposing full admin program-config records to unauthenticated visitors.
